---
title: "Native Calendar API protection"
description: "Trace timezone read/save rejection layers and audit the hosting exception without exposing credentials."
---

## Request ownership and counts

Native personal `/api/v1/users/calendar-settings` and workspace
`/api/v1/workspaces/:wsId/calendar-settings` GET/PATCH requests default directly to
Web at `https://tuturuuu.com` (`ApiOrigin.platform`, the existing Web origin). Web serves these paths locally;
its former Calendar rewrites must stay removed. `API_BASE_URL` and existing
origin overrides remain available for development and explicit environments.
The adapters inject the verified actor into shared calendar settings logic;
Calendar retains its routes for existing browser/app-session clients. Native
requests require the original Supabase Bearer token and verified MFA, without
a satellite browser session.

Infrastructure's `/api/v1/mobile-calendar` settings allowlist remains a deliberate
compatibility path for already published mobile versions. Those versions still
reach Calendar and still need the Calendar hosting exception below. The new
mobile release bypasses both hops only for these two preference endpoints;
other native Calendar APIs retain their current gateway routing. Shipping Web
alone cannot change the routing embedded in an installed mobile binary.

The app-level timezone scope makes one personal and one workspace GET at cold
startup. Opening/reopening Settings displays that scope and adds zero requests.
Same-workspace rebuilds do not reload. Account/workspace changes and OS resume
can revalidate; in-flight loads coalesce and 429 cooldown prevents replay.
Reminder planning separately reads preferences across workspaces; its bounded
traffic can consume a shared allowance but is not a Settings rebuild loop.

A valid unexpired access token does not refresh on each timezone read. Expiry
within the refresh buffer or a rejected 401 can cause a bounded refresh. Refresh
failure is a session error or falls back to an existing token; it is not itself
the API client's `kind=http; status=429` response. There is no automatic 429 retry.

## Rejection inventory

The Infrastructure/Calendar rows apply to the retained compatibility path. New
mobile preferences use Web hosting, the shared MFA/native-preferences guard and
the local Web adapter instead.

| Layer | Read/save protection and identity | Observable result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mobile repository | Account-scoped cooldown after a genuine 429; no network retry during cooldown | Retains the originating diagnostic; not proof of a fresh request on Settings open |
| Web hosting | Existing Web native API hosting policy; no WAF/bot exception is declared in `apps/web/vercel.json` | Provider challenges run before route auth; live policy must be checked by the deployment operator |
| Shared Web guard | Dedicated `proxy:web:calendar-preferences` actor bucket after MFA verification; persistent IP blocks | `native-calendar-preferences` with caller/window/quota headers; `proxy-ip-block` for blocked IPs |
| Web native integrity bridge GET guard | Exact `/native-integrity/turnstile` GET uses `proxy:web:native-integrity-bridge` with explicit base read limits of 60/minute, 240/hour and 1,200/day | `native-integrity-bridge`; anonymous IP limits, persistent IP blocks and strict staff rejection remain active |
| Web native integrity POST guard | Exact challenge/enroll POSTs use `proxy:web:native-integrity` with the already MFA-verified Bearer actor and default authenticated mutation quotas; no warm trust-cache dependency or shared-IP actor collision | `native-integrity-challenge`; anonymous quotas and persistent IP blocks remain active, and staff cannot waive quota/IP 429; separate service issuance caps remain 10/minute and 120/hour |
| Web personal PATCH quota | Additional adaptive authenticated actor quota using `session:user:mutate`, base 60/minute; no pre-auth shared-IP bucket or browser challenge | `calendar-session-user-mutate`, caller `authenticated`, window `minute`; preserves `Retry-After`, `X-Proxy-Block-Reason: rate-limit-exceeded`, `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, numeric `X-RateLimit-*` and adaptive `X-Abuse-*` headers |
| Infrastructure hosting | Platform bot/WAF/DDoS protections before application code | May return a bare HTML/JSON 429 without application metadata |
| Shared Infrastructure guard | Dedicated preferences quotas; already verified MFA Bearer actor, independent of warm trust cache | `native-calendar-preferences`, caller and minute/hour/day; IP blocks use `proxy-ip-block` |
| Offline download guard | Additional quotas only with explicit offline-download header | `offline-capable-read`; ordinary timezone startup does not mark bulk downloads |
| Infrastructure gateway authentication | Verifies original Bearer before secret access or fetch | Invalid/provider-rejected verification returns 401, unavailable verification 503, not raw 429 |
| Gateway upstream response | Single bounded fetch; relays JSON 429 and safe headers | Unclassified JSON 429 becomes `upstream-or-edge` / `calendar-upstream`; HTML challenges remain 502 |
| Calendar hosting | Bot protection and exact private-credential WAF exception | Native HTTP cannot complete a browser challenge; challenge can be HTML 429 |
| Shared Calendar guard | Dedicated native preferences actor quotas and persistent IP blocks | `calendar-native-preferences` or `proxy-ip-block` |
| Personal route session wrapper | GET has no session read quota. PATCH uses authenticated actor mutation quota; unrelated routes retain pre-auth IP quotas | `calendar-session-user-mutate`; old gateway-egress IP collision is covered by regression |
| Personal route IP/auth branches | Persistent IP-block policy; upstream Supabase Auth rejection | `calendar-route-ip-block` or `calendar-auth-provider`; unknown caller/window stay unknown |
| Workspace route | Explicit membership/settings permission; no additional route quota | Authentication failure 401, membership/permission 403; proxy quotas still apply |
| Supabase/PostgREST | Data API write hook keys authenticated user plus user/IP; GET/read-only transactions exempt; provider quotas remain | Settings handlers map data-query errors to 500, so these are not a bare settings GET 429 |

Default authenticated proxy read limits are 600/minute, 6,000/hour, 40,000/day;
mutation limits are 60/minute, 300/hour, 2,000/day. Personal and workspace paths
share each actor's quota across token rotation. Existing environment overrides,
trust/risk decisions, downstream authentication, MFA and IP blocks remain active.

## Web hosting acceptance and operator items

Application authentication and hosting bot protection are separate boundaries.
Existing native Web APIs use the shared Bearer/MFA guard; the documented browser
step-up policy excludes native clients. That does not establish an active Vercel
WAF exemption: `apps/web/vercel.json` contains no firewall rule. Do not add a fake
browser user agent or trust an unverified Authorization header to avoid hosting
challenges. [Vercel challenges require a browser session](https://vercel.com/docs/vercel-firewall/firewall-concepts#challenge-limitations).

The production operator must perform these steps; repository deployment does not
publish provider firewall configuration:

1. Confirm the deployed Web source includes local settings handlers and no
   Calendar settings rewrites. Read the active Web project's Firewall rules and
   pending draft privately. Identify the treatment already used for working
   native `/api/v1/**` calls on `tuturuuu.com`; check that both new exact paths
   receive the same treatment.
2. If Bot Protection challenges these paths, prepare a custom rule named
   `Native Web calendar preferences` with **all** these conditions: Host equals
   `tuturuuu.com`; Method is one of `GET`, `PATCH`; Path matches
   `^/api/v1/(users/calendar-settings|workspaces/[^/]+/calendar-settings)$`.
   Use the existing native Web hosting exception mechanism. If that mechanism
   is a Vercel custom **Bypass**, put it after applicable custom deny/rate rules
   and before managed bot evaluation. Review its full effect: Vercel custom
   Bypass skips all subsequent custom/managed rules, not just Bot Protection.
   Do not create a system bypass or broaden to all API paths. The path exception
   permits requests to reach application verification; it grants no actor trust.
   Retain platform DDoS protection, IP blocks and all application MFA, membership,
   permission and preference quotas. Review and publish only this scoped change
   through the release operator, then read back the active rule.
3. Verify both GET and PATCH with a real native client on the exact deployed
   source. Confirm JSON success, persistence and no `x-vercel-mitigated: challenge`.
   Confirm missing/forged Bearers fail, insufficient MFA fails, nonmembers and
   users without settings permission fail, invalid values fail, and controlled
   quota rejection retains `Retry-After` and `X-RateLimit-*` diagnostics. Keep
   private request identities out of reports. A curl control alone does not prove
   acceptance of an affected user's request.
4. Retain the existing Calendar private-credential rule for older mobile builds.
   The applied predicate coverage is recorded below; retain it and verify old-client
   read/save plus forged gateway credential rejection before calling that path
   recovered. Roll back the mobile origin only with the old route's hosting
   acceptance confirmed; otherwise it restores the original challenge exposure.

No live Vercel or Cloudflare firewall mutation is part of the source change.

## Compatibility gateway hosting exception coverage

The legacy native gateway WAF regex covered `/api/v1/calendar/**`, workspace
`/calendar/**` and the two cron routes, but excluded both `/calendar-settings`
endpoints. A matching private credential could therefore still encounter bot
protection on these reads/saves. `firewall-policy.test.ts` reproduces this exact
predicate gap and verifies the narrow correction without broadening other paths.

Save the owning Calendar project's active firewall response in a **private** file
using the authenticated Vercel CLI's read-only firewall API, then run:

```sh
bun scripts/audit-calendar-gateway-firewall.ts /private/path/calendar-firewall.json
```

The audit prints only public path predicates and coverage, never the gateway
credential. Exit 1 means missing coverage, 0 means both exact settings paths are
covered, and 2 means an unexpected rule or pending draft requires private review.
The audit cannot publish a firewall change.

The user-authoritative production review at **2026-10-24 02:02 UTC** confirms
the Calendar firewall correction is **applied**, configuration version **8**.
The read-only audit reported `current=true` for both exact calendar-settings
paths. This is an operator-provided configuration receipt, not a firewall
mutation performed by this source change or a fresh readback by this agent.
Do not reapply the correction blindly.

Retain the `Authenticated native Calendar gateway` rule's exact
`x-tuturuuu-calendar-gateway` credential equality, active bypass action and
corrected path predicate. Keep unrelated rules and managed bot protection.
Do not use mere Bearer presence as a hosting bypass. Future operator changes
must review any pending draft and read back the resulting active coverage.
Repository deployment alone does not publish provider configuration.

Remaining acceptance for the already published mobile version is real-device
personal/workspace GET and PATCH through the gateway, persistence, absence of a
Vercel challenge and forged-credential rejection. An audit's `current=true`
proves path coverage in that reviewed configuration, not successful device
behavior or attribution of the original affected request.

## Diagnostic interpretation

Older `diagnostics=v1` output with all four fields `unknown` cannot distinguish
absent headers from unsupported values. New diagnostics record metadata presence
and label a response with no limiter fields `upstream-or-edge`; that is a source
classification, not proof of a specific WAF/provider policy. Vercel/Cloudflare
header presence is a boolean, never a request ID, credential or arbitrary server
header. Known application rules retain their policy/caller/window and Retry-After.

Content negotiation matters: a Calendar request with `Accept: application/json`
and the gateway's Node user agent can receive a **JSON** 429 with
`x-vercel-mitigated: challenge` and no application quota fields. The gateway
relays that JSON status; the legacy missing settings-path exception therefore
provides a concrete mechanism for the device's all-unknown 429 fingerprint.
HTML challenges instead become 502. The fixed gateway preserves only the exact
safe `challenge` marker and classifies unlabelled upstream JSON rejections.
An unauthenticated control does not establish the affected user's individual
request receipt. Correlate that build's effective host/path and timestamp with
Infrastructure/Calendar logs to attribute an exact event. Keep the private
credential condition: direct requests without it should still be challenged.
Never log tokens, cookies, private bodies, actor/workspace identifiers or IPs here.


## Native integrity rollout (default off)

Phase 1 moves the preference endpoints to Web independently of native integrity.
Ship that routing repair first; integrity is a separate dependent change. It adds
Apple App Attest, Android Play Integrity STANDARD requests and a bounded
Turnstile fallback. These proofs supplement Bearer authentication, MFA,
workspace membership/permissions, dedicated quotas and IP blocks. They never
replace those controls or grant a hosting firewall bypass.

`NATIVE_INTEGRITY_MODE` is a server-side rollout control. Only `monitor` and
`enforce` opt in; unset or unrecognized values resolve to `off`:

| Mode | Integrity behavior | Existing API behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `off` (default, including an unset value) | No integrity datastore/provider calls or proof requirement | Existing authentication, quotas and permissions remain authoritative |
| `monitor` | Verify available proofs and record only scalar mode/mechanism/verdict; missing, malformed, unsupported, provider/configuration/store errors do not block the protected request | Always continue through existing protections; a valid proof grants no quota/auth bypass |
| `enforce` | Require a valid request-bound proof before domain writes | A missing/failed proof returns `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_REQUIRED`; only the release operator may enable this after acceptance |

No production enforcement change is implied by merging the implementation.
Monitor is not evidence that every platform/device can satisfy enforce. An old
mobile binary has no proof support, so enforcing globally before its support
policy is settled would block that client.

**Enforce activation is blocked by existing Web callers too.** The current guard
applies to every authenticated Web calendar-settings GET/PATCH, including calls
with no integrity header. Existing browser/server consumers such as
`apps/web/src/components/settings/appearance-settings.tsx` and
`apps/web/src/lib/calendar-preferences-settings-bridge.tsx` do not yet supply
proofs and would receive 403 in enforce. Keep `off` or `monitor` until those
callers have accepted proof coverage or a separately reviewed trusted-browser
policy is implemented and accepted. Never exempt a caller merely because its
header is absent or its User-Agent claims to be a browser. This implementation
is not a fully activated rollout.

### Configuration names

All provider secrets remain in Web's server secret store. Mobile learns public
challenge configuration from the authenticated server response; never inject a
service-account key or Turnstile secret into Flutter. There is no separate mobile
rollout flag: the authenticated challenge response discovers the server mode.
An `off` response invokes no device verifier or widget.

| Server variable | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_MODE` | `off`, `monitor`, or operator-approved `enforce` |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_WEB_ORIGIN` | Exact bridge origin; defaults to `https://tuturuuu.com` |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_TURNSTILE_ENABLED` | Literal `true` enables consideration of fallback; disabled by default |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM_ACTOR_IDS` | Operator-owned UUID allowlist for unsupported actors, maximum 500; native capability still bars fallback |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_PROVIDER_BUDGET_ACTOR_DAY` | Per-actor daily provider budget, default 100 and capped at one tenth of global budget |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_TURNSTILE_PARENT_ORIGINS` | Up to 16 comma-separated approved exact HTTPS parent origins, including Web by default; loopback HTTP only in development |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_APPLE_IOS_ACL_BLOBS` | Explicit comma-separated base64 iOS ACL allowlist from official or controlled signed-device evidence; unknown ACL fails verification |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_APPLE_BUNDLE_ID` | Expected Apple app identity |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_APPLE_ALLOWED_BUNDLE_VERSIONS` | Required accepted iOS bundle versions when signed launch extensions are present |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_APPLE_MACOS_BUNDLE_ID`, `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_APPLE_MACOS_SIGNING_IDENTIFIER`, `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_APPLE_MACOS_ALLOWED_BUNDLE_VERSIONS` | Explicit macOS app identity/signing identifier and required accepted bundle versions |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_PROVIDER_ENABLED`, `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_PROVIDER_BUDGET_DAY` | Provider stop control and total daily dispatch budget (default 1,000, range 2–100,000) |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_APPLE_ENVIRONMENT` | Development attestation is allowed only when explicitly set to `development`; production is the release default |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_GOOGLE_PACKAGE_NAME`, `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_GOOGLE_CERTIFICATE_DIGESTS` | Expected Android package and comma-separated signing certificate digests |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_NUMBER` | Linked project's public number for STANDARD requests |
| `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` | Server-only Google decoder credentials |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY`, `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` | Widget public key and server-only Siteverify secret |
| `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL`, `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` | Server-only atomic challenge/key store connection |

### Request and fallback contract

Native App Attest and Play Integrity proofs are accepted across an actor's
devices. A Turnstile token is a bot-abuse speed bump, not native app/device
attestation and not evidence equivalent to either native mechanism. Fallback is
disabled by default: only the literal `true` in
`NATIVE_INTEGRITY_TURNSTILE_ENABLED` enables consideration of it. It additionally
requires server-owned eligibility in
`NATIVE_INTEGRITY_UNSUPPORTED_PLATFORM_ACTOR_IDS`, a comma-separated UUID
allowlist capped at 500 actors. Headers, User-Agent claims and the absence of a
native proof cannot grant unsupported-platform eligibility.

A live enrolled Apple capability or a successful Play capability marker takes
precedence over that allowlist and bars Turnstile for the actor. Native App
Attest and Play proofs still work across that actor's Apple/Android devices;
the restriction is against downgrading a native-capable actor to Turnstile.
The Play marker expires 90 days after the most recent verified Play proof.
Do not clear capability state simply to make a denied fallback succeed.

The authenticated client obtains a short-lived challenge from
`POST /api/v1/native-integrity/challenge`; Apple key enrollment uses
`POST /api/v1/native-integrity/enroll`. Proofs accompany the protected request in
`x-tuturuuu-integrity-proof` (base64url JSON), with the mechanism identified by
`x-tuturuuu-native-integrity`. Do not log either header.

A single-use nonce expires after 120 seconds and binds the authenticated actor
and intended request. The server validates the proof against the actual method,
path and request data; the client cannot nominate another actor. Apple enrollment
verifies the Apple certificate chain, app identity and attestation environment,
then stores the verified key and platform for assertions. Modern Apple ACL
extensions require accepted platform-specific evidence. An iOS ACL blob is
allowed only by the explicit configured allowlist; never promote an arbitrary
client capture into that list. macOS requires the published SIP/full-security
ACL and matching signing identifier/version policy. Unknown macOS ACLs fail
verification; they cannot downgrade into the iOS assertion path. Assertions must pass signature,
request binding and a strictly increasing counter. Android STANDARD token
verification compares the request hash, package and configured signing certificate
digests, requires `PLAY_RECOGNIZED`, `LICENSED` and `MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY`,
and rejects a verdict older than 120 seconds.

Only when fallback is enabled and the server-owned eligibility policy allows
it does `/native-integrity/turnstile` provide the WebView fallback. Its bridge is locked
to the expected Web origin, page path and request hash. Native WebViews read a
bounded top-document result; the browser iframe validates both `event.origin`
and its owned frame's `event.source`. Tokens and access credentials must never
escape through navigation, logs or arbitrary JavaScript messages. The page receives no Bearer
token. Server verification checks the configured hostname, action
`native_integrity` and nonce-bound `cData` in addition to Siteverify success.
Turnstile tokens are [single use and expire after five minutes](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/get-started/server-side-validation/);
the tighter server nonce lifetime still applies. Reads, workspace loads and
retries require their own proofs, not a reusable CAPTCHA session credential.

Enrollment exposes only `verified` to the client; detailed reason codes remain
in scalar server diagnostics. A monitor-allowed failure is not verified enrollment.

Monitor continues through existing protections even if fallback is unavailable.
An eligible enforce client may perform only a bounded fallback attempt after an explicit
pre-write integrity rejection; a transport timeout is an unknown write outcome,
not permission to replay a PATCH. Do not run a background verification loop or
retry provider calls indefinitely. An invisible widget can still fail or need
user recovery. [Cloudflare requires a WebView for native integration](https://developers.cloudflare.com/turnstile/get-started/mobile-implementation/).

### Apple operator setup

1. Confirm the Apple App ID prefix/team and each shipped bundle identifier;
   configure the matching server app identity separately for development and
   distribution. Accepted iOS bundle-version lists are mandatory for signed
   launch extensions; macOS always requires its accepted bundle-version list. Configure the macOS bundle and
   signing identifiers explicitly; do not assume the iOS profile validates macOS.
   Use Apple's App Attest root certificate as the trust anchor.
   An App ID prefix must be verified rather than assumed equal to the team ID.
2. Enable App Attest for the App ID/capability and regenerate the appropriate
   provisioning profiles. Include
   `com.apple.developer.devicecheck.appattest-environment` with the intended
   development/production environment in the signed app entitlement. Inspect
   the built distribution artifact and profile; a source entitlement alone is
   not delivery evidence. Capture the expected iOS ACL only from official or
   controlled signed-device evidence and review it before configuring
   `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_APPLE_IOS_ACL_BLOBS`. Unknown ACLs remain failure verdicts;
   use an eligible fresh-challenge fallback or monitor outcome rather than
   weakening validation.
3. Exercise `DCAppAttestService.isSupported` on real iOS 14+ devices and the
   shipped macOS target. The macOS channel requires macOS 27+ and its supported
   SDK/compiler guard (Swift 6.4); older targets require the server-owned
   unsupported-platform fallback policy or continue without proof in monitor. OS/API availability
   and runtime support are both required; do not classify simulators or
   unsupported devices as verified. Keep their fallback/monitor behavior explicit.
4. The client keeps the opaque key identifier and enrollment marker in secure
   storage scoped by a hash of Web origin and actor, with 30-day key rotation.
   Sign-out retains this actor-scoped state; another actor cannot adopt it.
   Successful enrollment must be server-confirmed before marking it locally.
   Never persist a private key or attestation token in ordinary preferences.
   Test re-enrollment after key loss, reinstall and account deletion/switching;
   the server must not reassign another actor's enrolled key. Keep development
   and production enrollments separate.

Follow [Apple's integrity setup](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/establishing-your-app-s-integrity)
and [server validation guide](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/devicecheck/validating-apps-that-connect-to-your-server).

### Android operator setup

1. Enable Play Integrity API in the intended Google Cloud project and link that
   project to the app in Play Console > Protected with Play > Play Integrity API.
   Use the linked project's number for STANDARD token preparation.
2. Create a dedicated server service account in that project. Grant only the
   decode capability required for this app/project and use the `playintegrity`
   OAuth scope; do not grant project Owner/Editor or release publishing access
   to solve a decode error. Verify the service identity can decode for the exact
   package while unrelated app/project access fails. Store credentials in server-only
   `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_GOOGLE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON`, never a mobile build define or
   repository file.
3. Configure the expected package name and Play App Signing certificate digest
   from the distributed artifact. Review required app-recognition, licensing and
   device-integrity verdicts against the release policy. Test a Play-installed
   release, debug/sideloaded build, unsupported device, expiry, changed request
   hash, reused token and provider outage. Do not silently relax verdicts to
   turn a failed negative control green.
4. Check actual API quota/usage before monitor traffic. Bound provider requests
   and retries, measure decoder error/latency, and obtain any quota increase
   before enforcement depends on it.

See [Play Integrity setup](https://developer.android.com/google/play/integrity/setup)
and [STANDARD requests and server decoding](https://developer.android.com/google/play/integrity/standard).

### Turnstile and state operator setup

Unsupported Apple targets and Linux/Windows/browser clients may use the bounded
Turnstile path only under the explicit server-owned fallback policy above. A
failed native proof or unsupported client claim does not itself grant eligibility. Desktop WebView operation requires the
platform runtime: Linux WebKitGTK 4.1/libsoup3 and Windows WebView2. Verify those
prerequisites on the shipped desktop target; their presence on a development
host is not device acceptance.

Configure the approved Turnstile site key and exact allowed Web hostname for the
bridge, plus the server-only secret. Configure only the accepted exact parent
origins in `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_TURNSTILE_PARENT_ORIGINS`; the bridge CSP and the
narrow Next framing exception must agree. Verify action `native_integrity`, expected
hostname and nonce-derived `cData` with a real hosted widget. Do not copy a secret
into Flutter, expose it in page source or use a broad domain/navigation allowlist.

Use `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL` and `UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN` from the server
secret store for atomic nonce issuance/consumption and Apple key/counter updates.
Verify concurrent replay admits at most one request and counter comparisons
cannot race across workers. Stored verification records require private access
controls and deletion handling. Never restore an old counter/nonce snapshot
into enforcement without reconciling replay state.

Each protected API call needs its own challenge; enrollment and a permitted
fresh-challenge fallback consume additional issuance capacity. The service caps
are 10 challenges per actor/minute and 120/hour. Two preference reads, repeated
saves, multiple devices, enrollment and fallback can consume this allowance.
Observe monitor-mode traffic and failure coverage before enforcement; tune only
through an owned reviewed change, preserving bounded operations rather than
silently broadening caps or adding retry loops.

Apple registration is capped at eight live keys per actor and uses a 90-day
non-sliding retention period; counter updates preserve the expiry. Mobile key
rotation is 30 days. Multiple devices and retained rotation history can reach
the eight-key cap. Accept a deliberate old-key revocation/re-enrollment policy,
verify lost-device and account-deletion handling, and do not evict keys blindly
while in-flight assertions may depend on them. The global key-owner fence
prevents registration of one key to another actor. The bounded actor revocation
helper removes at most eight Apple key records, their matching owner records,
and the Play capability marker (at most nine actor records). Its caller must
first authorize actor deletion. Exporting the helper is not evidence that the
account-deletion flow invokes it end to end; retain that enforcement gate.
Outstanding challenges expire within 120 seconds and remain actor/request bound.

Provider dispatch is bounded by the global UTC daily
`NATIVE_INTEGRITY_PROVIDER_BUDGET_DAY` (default 1,000, minimum two, maximum
100,000) and per-actor `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_PROVIDER_BUDGET_ACTOR_DAY` (default 100,
capped at one tenth of the global budget). A cold OAuth exchange plus Play
decode reserves two units; cached OAuth plus decode reserves one, as does
Siteverify. Each actual dispatch reserves atomically before network work; failed
or unknown outcomes retain reservations. A durable daily warning logs once at
80% before exhaustion. Verify operation-count, per-actor isolation and restart
behavior in the real store. Provider calls have no automatic retries.
`NATIVE_INTEGRITY_PROVIDER_ENABLED=false` stops new provider dispatch; the
Redis `native-integrity:v1:provider-stop` value `1` is the durable stop fence.
Clearing that fence does not reset consumed daily budgets.

Nonce consumption and counter advancement remain atomic; no consumed challenge
is restored after an invalid proof. Play OAuth, decode and response reading
share a maximum five-second deadline; Siteverify fetch/body reading share its
bounded deadline. Cancellation tests cover compliant providers/streams, not
arbitrary injected promises that ignore abort/cancel.

The Turnstile bridge retains the shared proxy IP/rate checks. Operator hosting
acceptance must cover exact challenge/enroll POSTs, bridge GET and protected
settings paths. The exact issuance POST guard reuses the already MFA-verified
actor in `proxy:web:native-integrity`; its diagnostic policy is
`native-integrity-challenge`. Anonymous limits, persistent IP blocks and strict
staff rejection remain active. Attestation never bypasses an upstream Vercel
challenge that rejects a request before application execution.

### Third-party mobile supplier provenance

The mobile dependency is third-party `app_attest` 0.2.1, not an official Apple
or Google SDK wrapper publication. Its official pub.dev archive SHA-256 is
`4ef28bc63690337abbde35d5eb075030d645a591c932e8db0490ce54f2ce5755`.
The reviewed archive matches the lockfile/cache digest; all 19 published files
matched immutable repository commit
`a2968d2d49d6ad6a888b679720835f6a0ea6aa16` (published 2026-08-03).
The repository has no release tag for the reviewed publication, its commit is
unsigned and the pub uploader is unverified; no signed publisher attestation
was found. These are provenance limits, not proof that a provider rejected it.

The reviewed Android StandardPlayIntegrityClient.kt uses
`IntegrityManagerFactory.createStandard`, prepares with the Cloud project
number, and passes the trimmed incoming request hash to
`StandardIntegrityTokenRequest.setRequestHash` before `provider.request`.
The canonical 43-character base64url request hash is passed unchanged and is
not rehashed by this wrapper. Its Gradle dependency pins
`com.google.android.play:integrity:1.4.0`.

Sources: [pub.dev publication](https://pub.dev/packages/app_attest/versions/0.2.1),
[immutable source commit](https://github.com/m0t1p4n/app_attest/commit/a2968d2d49d6ad6a888b679720835f6a0ea6aa16),
[Android STANDARD adapter](https://github.com/m0t1p4n/app_attest/blob/a2968d2d49d6ad6a888b679720835f6a0ea6aa16/android/src/main/kotlin/com/motsipan/StandardPlayIntegrityClient.kt).

### Acceptance and rollback

1. Ship and verify phase 1 Web routing first. Keep integrity `off` while exact
   commit builds, real-provider configuration and signed device artifacts are
   checked. Existing Calendar hosting exceptions remain required for old clients.
   The operator must also confirm native access to challenge/enroll POSTs and
   the hosted bridge GET; accepting only the protected settings paths is
   insufficient. Keep hosting exceptions narrow by exact path/method and retain
   authentication/quota checks on issuance and enrollment.
2. Enable `monitor` only through the release operator. Measure supported-client
   coverage, mechanism/verdict counts, fallback frequency, provider/store errors,
   latency, nonce replay/expiry, counter conflicts and request volume. Keep
   metrics scalar/aggregated; never log actor, workspace, IP, path, request hash,
   key ID, token, proof or credential values in integrity diagnostics.
3. Accept real iOS/Android/macOS or intentional unsupported-platform fallback,
   valid/invalid proofs, wrong actor/request, replay, expiry, concurrent requests,
   outage/cancellation and existing auth/MFA/quota/permission failures. Decide
   the old-client and sideload policy before the operator considers `enforce`.
4. Enable `enforce` only for the accepted scope with a rollout owner and rollback
   receipt. Set `NATIVE_INTEGRITY_MODE=off` to stop requiring proofs and stop
   integrity datastore/provider work; preserve existing API protection. Verify
   rollback on the deployed configuration, not merely a local flag fixture.

Unit tests with synthetic certificates/provider responses establish the covered
verification logic only. Real provider, hosted bridge, entitlement/provisioning,
Play Console and signed-device acceptance require operator configuration and
have not been established by those fixtures. Attestation or Turnstile in Web
cannot bypass a Vercel challenge that stops the request before code executes;
the hosting operator checklist above still applies.

  [`server.test.ts`](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/packages/turnstile/src/server.test.ts).

Phase 1 preference routing and authorization regressions:

- Shared validation, persistence, defaults, membership and edit permission:
  [`calendar-settings-server.test.ts`](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/packages/internal-api/src/calendar-settings-server.test.ts).
- Web auth/MFA and response contract:
  [`calendar-settings-handler.test.ts`](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/apps/web/src/lib/calendar-settings-handler.test.ts).
- Web personal PATCH adaptive actor quota and diagnostic parity:
  [`calendar-personal-mutation-quota.test.ts`](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/apps/web/src/lib/calendar-personal-mutation-quota.test.ts).
- Web guard route boundaries, dedicated quotas and diagnostic parity:
  [`calendar-preference-guard.test.ts`](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/apps/web/src/lib/calendar-preference-guard.test.ts),
  plus `api-proxy-calendar-preference-reads.test.ts` and
  `api-proxy-calendar-preference-mutations.test.ts` in the same directory.
- Web local ownership rather than Calendar forwarding:
  [`satellite-api-rewrites.test.ts`](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/apps/web/src/lib/satellite-api-rewrites.test.ts).
- Mobile direct Web routing and environment overrides:
  [`api_origins_test.dart`](https://github.com/tutur3u/platform/blob/main/apps/mobile/test/core/config/api_origins_test.dart).
- Retained old-client gateway and private-credential WAF coverage:
  `apps/infrastructure/src/lib/mobile-calendar/gateway.test.ts` and
  `firewall-policy.test.ts`.

These tests establish source behavior at their tested boundaries. Exact-commit
CI builds, deployed hosting policy and real native read/save acceptance remain
separate release evidence.

## Retained Web and Tasks Google sync helpers

The `apps/web` and `apps/tasks` copies of
`src/lib/calendar/incremental-active-sync.ts` log sync-token presence and page
counts, never the stored sync token or the raw Google page response containing
`nextSyncToken`. This scope is separate from the native gateway and Calendar's
current provider-sync implementation.

For a Google error with numeric `code: 410` during incremental fetching, these
helpers increment `retryCount`, disable token use and attempt to clear the token
under the same workspace/connection/calendar key. Clear failures are logged and
swallowed. Despite the retry counter, a first-page 410 exits the pagination loop
without a date-range request because no `pageToken` exists. After a successful
clear, the next invocation fetches the configured date range without a sync token
and stores a returned replacement token, including for an empty event page.
This is a bounded date-range fetch, not a complete calendar-history rebuild.

A later-page 410 retains the existing page cursor and accumulated events while
switching to date-range parameters; it does not restart pagination. A 410 already
in date-range mode, or another Google error, propagates without token recovery.
The sibling `incremental-active-sync.test.ts` suites exercise the real helpers
with mocked Google and storage boundaries: token-free logs, pagination/storage,
first-page 410 clearing and next-invocation fetching, and non-410 propagation.
They do not prove live Google acceptance, clear-failure recovery, later-page
recovery correctness, or database event-write behavior.
